English: I'm staying at home because I **am** ill.
German: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank **bin**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: weil sends the verb to the very end of its clause.

English: He isn't coming because he **has** to work.
German: Er kommt nicht, weil er arbeiten **muss**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: With a modal, the modal itself goes last, after the infinitive.

English: I'm learning German because my girlfriend **comes** from Berlin.
German: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil meine Freundin aus Berlin **kommt**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The subject stays right after weil; only the verb moves to the end.

English: We're eating now because we **are** hungry.
German: Wir essen jetzt, weil wir Hunger **haben**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: weil … haben: the verb last.

English: She is tired because she **works** a lot.
German: Sie ist müde, weil sie viel **arbeitet**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: A comma always comes before weil.

English: Why are you laughing? (one friend) – Because the film **is** so funny.
German: Warum lachst du? – Weil der Film so lustig **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: A weil clause can answer warum on its own; the verb is still last.

English: I'm taking the bus because it **is raining**.
German: Ich nehme den Bus, weil es **regnet**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: weil es regnet: the verb at the end.

English: Because I **am** tired, I'm going home.
German: Weil ich müde **bin**, gehe ich nach Hause.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The whole weil clause takes the first place, so the main verb comes straight after the comma: gehe ich.

English: I'm waiting here because my sister **is picking** me **up**.
German: Ich warte hier, weil meine Schwester mich **abholt**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: At the end of a clause, a separable verb is one word again: abholt.

English: I'm learning German because it **is** fun.
German: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil es Spaß **macht**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Spaß machen: to be fun. macht goes last.

English: I'm not coming because I **have** a headache.
German: Ich komme nicht, weil ich Kopfschmerzen **habe**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Kopfschmerzen, plural in German. habe last.

English: I think that the restaurant **is** good.
German: Ich glaube, dass das Restaurant gut **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: dass also sends the verb to the end. English can drop that; German keeps dass.

English: I know that you **have** no time. (one friend)
German: Ich weiß, dass du keine Zeit **hast**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: dass du … hast: the verb last.

English: I **know** that he lives here.
German: Ich **weiß**, dass er hier wohnt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wissen is irregular: ich weiß, with no ending, and er weiß too.

English: She says that she **is coming** tomorrow.
German: Sie sagt, dass sie morgen **kommt**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Reported speech with dass: the verb at the end.

English: We hope the weather **is** nice tomorrow.
German: Wir hoffen, dass das Wetter morgen schön **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: hoffen, dass…: the verb last.

English: Do you know that the bus **isn't running** today? (one friend)
German: Weißt du, dass der Bus heute nicht **fährt**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: nicht stays just before the verb at the end.

English: I'm sure that he **can** come.
German: Ich bin sicher, dass er kommen **kann**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The modal goes last: kommen kann.

English: He thinks the exam **is** easy.
German: Er meint, dass die Prüfung leicht **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: meinen: to think, to have an opinion.

English: I hope you **pass** the exam. (one friend)
German: Ich hoffe, dass du die Prüfung **bestehst**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: eine Prüfung bestehen: to pass an exam. bestehst last.

English: I didn't know that you **smoke**. (one friend)
German: Ich habe nicht gewusst, dass du **rauchst**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The main clause is in the perfect; the dass clause still ends with its verb.

English: I know that I **have** to learn more.
German: Ich weiß, dass ich mehr lernen **muss**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The modal last, after the infinitive.

English: If it **rains**, we'll stay at home.
German: Wenn es **regnet**, bleiben wir zu Hause.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn sends the verb to the end; then the main verb follows straight after the comma.

English: If you **have** time, call me. (one friend)
German: Wenn du Zeit **hast**, ruf mich an.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn … hast, then the imperative.

English: If the sun **is shining**, we'll go swimming.
German: Wenn die Sonne **scheint**, gehen wir schwimmen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: gehen + infinitive: to go and do something.

English: When I **am** tired, I drink coffee.
German: Wenn ich müde **bin**, trinke ich Kaffee.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn also means when, for something that happens every time.

English: If you **want**, you can come along. (one friend)
German: Wenn du **willst**, kannst du mitkommen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn du willst: the verb last, then kannst right after the comma.

English: I go by bike when the weather **is** nice.
German: Ich fahre mit dem Fahrrad, wenn das Wetter schön **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The wenn clause can also come second.

English: If you **are** ill, you have to go to the doctor. (formal)
German: Wenn Sie krank **sind**, müssen Sie zum Arzt gehen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn … sind, then müssen Sie.

English: If you **feel like** it, we can dance. (one friend)
German: Wenn du Lust **hast**, können wir tanzen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Lust haben: to feel like doing something.
